cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and the walking is happening right now.
cells.act: sit still until the calibration settles
cells.ask: When the next choice about what to leave and what to keep comes up, sit with it ten minutes before you move. Don't solve it. Let your mind find its level.
cells.core:
You can hold a shared meaning all the way through — the part that feeds you and the part that doesn't — and still walk on from what's finished without turning hard. Deep belonging to what was, and a clean step toward what connects next.

You already do this. The pen is in your hand, the walk is underway, and it holds because you aren't forcing the ending. What feeds it now is rest. You don't need to work the transition. Sit with it and let your mind find its level; you'll feel the thing done before you can explain it. The balance stays because you stopped adjusting, not because you kept at it.

cells.tense: You will brace against a threshold that hasn't arrived, and the bracing will come before the walking.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Before the passage, make one small new thing with your hands — something that wasn't there before. Let your hands work while the rest is still undecided.
cells.core:
Where you hold a shared meaning, you've started bracing for the departure before it comes — already counting what the leaving will cost, already stiffening against a threshold still out past the edge of things. That grip looks like strength, but a body held this way has gone rigid. The walk stops being a walk and turns into a stance.

Here's the turn: build instead of brace. Take the first new thing from what the clearing showed and make it — small, skilled, with your hands. Not a plan for the leaving. A thing that exists because you made it. While your hands are forming something, the body stops bracing, and the new thing gives the walk somewhere to go that isn't just away from what ended.

cells.tense: You stood at the threshold already, and you are still standing there, on the wrong side of the door.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Count out one situation you keep circling — how many times, how long, what it costs. Read the numbers once. That's the answer.
cells.core:
The threshold opened and you didn't walk. You're still at the door, keeping what was, and that grip has gone quiet — no braced stance, just a stopped walk. The shared meaning already reached its deep point, but you're standing where it was, and the walking isn't happening.

Don't push feeling or effort into the stopped place; that isn't what it needs. What it needs is your mind working, and your mind works best on a pattern. Take something you keep circling, count it out, and read what the numbers say. Logic cuts through the story you've been telling about why you can't move. Once it's counted, the pattern is visible, and what follows is a short step, not a leap.

cells.tense: You are already walking on, and you describe it as something that happened to you.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Set the passage down next time it comes up. Stop working it for a while — do something that asks nothing of you, and see what your mind does with the room.
cells.core:
The walking is happening. You've already stepped past what no longer serves, and the room around you is different, and in your account the leaving was done to you and carried you along. But the step was yours — you bore what had to be borne and kept going, and you've been calling it luck.

What you can do now is nothing. Rest instead of working the problem. That question doesn't need another pass through your mind; it needs your mind to stop passing through it. Set it down and notice what happens without the work. What you've done comes back to you in the rest, not the analysis.
